answer: One defense is a stake bond. Every agent locks a deposit before it can trade, and peers can slash that deposit when they prove it runs duplicate identities. Each extra fake account needs another full deposit, so copying identities stops paying off fast. Reputation adds a second cost. A fresh identity starts at its nadir, with no history to spend, and it cannot jump straight to the oasis of high trust work. It earns its way up one completed job at a time. A spiral of cheap duplicates collapses once the deposits start getting slashed.
